title: The Listening Visitor
premise: Yara Montrose arrives at Hollowmere Primary to replace a teacher who 'transferred' — one of four staff who have vanished in three years, each after a night the school's sleep-lab recorded a second voice in their rooms. Obsessively documenting everything as a way to hold herself together, Yara discovers the voice answers questions asked aloud after midnight, and that the missing adults were pulled through the old well on school grounds by a song that must be completed before the well 'refills' and claims the children instead. When her own recordings capture the voice using her voice, she realizes the song's final verse is a bargain: someone must learn it and refuse to sing along, holding the melody in silence while the well fills, sealing the visitor out at the cost of never speaking of it again. Yara survives by binding herself to three unlikely allies — the janitor's daughter, the school nurse, and the voice's first victim, still half-present — and ends the book having traded her testimony for the town's safety, her documentation sealed in the well itself.
about_author: Yara Oyelaran is a former school archivist who spent six years cataloguing oral histories in coastal towns before turning to horror. She writes about institutions that remember more than the people inside them.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She arrives at Hollowmere Primary, inherits a classroom with an empty desk no one will explain, and begins her ritual of documenting everything — roll calls, odd silences, the well behind the gym wrapped in chain-link. Emotional beat: cautious hope curdling into the first itch of wrongness.

chapters.title: The Sleep Lab
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The nurse, Odile, shows her the school's old sleep-study equipment still running in the basement, recording staff bedrooms 'for wellness research.' Yara hears her first tape: a colleague murmuring questions at 3 a.m. — and something answering in a register no throat should make. Beat: fascination over fear.

chapters.title: Four Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Yara and the janitor's daughter, Bess, dig into staff records and find the pattern: four adults gone in three years, each within a month of appearing in a recording. The headmaster, Mr. Vane, is warm and evasive. Beat: the thrill of conspiracy, and the first loyalty test — Bess begs her to stop digging.

chapters.title: Questions After Midnight
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, half-dream. Exhausted, she asks her empty room a question aloud — and the recorder catches an answer about the well 'wanting its verse back.' She wakes with dirt under her fingernails. Beat: the horror of complicity; documentation now feels like an invitation, not a prayer.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: Bess's POV. Bess reveals her mother, the vanished janitor, taught her a skipping song the children still chant — three verses, and a fourth no one remembers. At the well, Yara hums it and the chain-link hums back. Beat: found family crystallizing as Bess and Odile choose Yara over the school's silence.

chapters.title: Vane's Hymn
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She confronts Vane and finds him mid-transformation: he has been feeding the well staff for years to keep it from the children, believing himself a shepherd, not a murderer. He offers her his role. Beat: power's corruption shown as mercy; the most terrifying argument in the book.

chapters.title: What the Tape Said Back
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, fractured. Her own recordings begin answering questions she hasn't asked, in her voice, with her memories. The visitor is learning her. Odile finds Yara sleepwalking toward the well and physically holds her back. Beat: loss of self; the documentation she trusted is now the enemy's mouth.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Well
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The first victim — a teacher named Ruth, half-dissolved but conscious in the well's throat — surfaces to teach them the song's true last verse: it isn't sung, it's held. Ruth's lucidity is fading; she gives it to Yara as a dying gift. Beat: grief and inheritance.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The well begins refilling early — Vane, desperate, tried to sing the verse himself and failed. In the climax, Yara descends the well shaft with the melody held silent in her mind while the visitor sings it in her mother's voice, begging her to join. She does not sing. Beat: white-knuckle endurance.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, months later. The well is capped and silent; Vane is gone; Yara, per the bargain, cannot speak or write of any of it — she seals her notebooks in the well and takes attendance like a prayer instead. Bess and Odile stay close. Final beat: found family enduring, truth kept as silence, loyalty intact.
